main_text.p: consultum fuisse de voce confirmari in ordine Romano ubi agitur de Communicantibus Christi sangvini, patet ex ejusdē Nihusii ad illū Epistola. Liber Maimonidæ, de cujus autoritate inqvisivit Morinus, videtur esse ille, qvi inscribitur jad ha zaca [?] seu manus fortis, & est absolutissimum Doctrinæ Talmudicæ compendium, qvod hodie māgni fit à Judæis ; etsi initio Doctrina Judæi illius á sectæ suæ magistris severius reprehensa fuerit, qvod veluti paternarum traditionum desertor Philosophiæ Peripaticæ Sophismata in Judaicam Religionem invexisset, maximè in opere cui nomen fecit, more nevo-kim seu Doctor perplexorum. Qvid à Morino observatum fuerit de erroribus jam annotatis in contextu Hebræo & Chaldæo Polyglottorum Parisiensium, nescio ; at notum est omnibus, Flavignium Doctorem Sorbonicum & Regium in Academia Parisiensi Linguæ Hebrææ profesorem gravissime ea de re conquestum fuisse, magnaqve disidia inter eos, qvi huic editioni præerant,

page.notes: The Hebrew words "jad ha zaca" are printed in Latin letters in italic, not in Hebrew script; the word "zaca" has a letter-form that is unclear and is marked [?]. The right side of the scan shows a dark smudge and show-through, which is not printed text. The running head is printed with the page number "107" at the top right.
